outroLine: Login, path, transport — proven before it matters.

beats.shot: Delivery tab with a SAVED SFTP config (host/port/path prefilled). Cursor touches the SFTP protocol card, rests on host + port, types the username.
beats.vo: When a supplier takes orders as files instead of over an A P I, ProcuLink drops the finished order file on their server over S F T P or F T P S. This supplier is already set up — host, port, and a username for the account they gave you.

beats.shot: Cursor rests on the Auth method select (Password), the masked password field (********), and the 'saved credential masked' badge.
beats.vo: Authentication is a password, or a private key. This config has a saved password — notice it's shown only as a mask. Secrets are write-only: encrypted at rest, never displayed back, and saving with the field left blank keeps the stored one.

beats.shot: Auth method switched to Private key: the key textarea reveals (with the product's own refuse-to-keep-a-wrong-shape-secret notice), and an OpenSSH-style sample key is typed in.
beats.vo: Private key is the stronger and more common choice for S F T P. The supplier registers your public key, and the matching private key is pasted here — in OpenSSH P E M form, the kind that begins BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY — header lines and all.

beats.shot: A key-formats note card (overlay): OpenSSH PEM = the expected form; a PuTTY .ppk container is best exported to OpenSSH via PuTTYgen first. The passphrase field sits below in the real form.
beats.vo: If your key lives in PuTTY's dot p p k container, the safest route is to open it in PuTTYgen once and export an OpenSSH key, then paste that. And if the key is protected by a passphrase, it goes in the field right below.

beats.shot: Cursor rests on Remote path, then the 'Create the remote directory if it does not exist' checkbox (ticked). Protocol switched to FTPS; rest on the 'Allow invalid TLS certificate' caution toggle (off).
beats.vo: The remote path is where the file lands. Leave create-directory ticked and ProcuLink makes the folder when it's missing — untick it if the server insists the path already exists. On F T P S, certificate checks stay on by default; allow an invalid certificate only for a supplier you've confirmed runs a self-signed host.

beats.shot: Back on SFTP; cursor rests on the enabled Test-fire button (never clicked — no mock backend).
beats.vo: Then prove the route with a test-fire. A green test means the login worked, the path resolved, and a test file was written. A delivered file is still not an accepted order — the supplier's system can reject the contents downstream, and ProcuLink reports those as separate steps.
